**Ruling from the user:** clean up the tests and remove every test that does not test business logic or does not add real value; the user says we have an excessive number. Your scope is the Angular Vitest suite in `web/src`, about 243 tests.

**Setup:** in your worktree, run `git checkout -B tests-prune-web main`. Then run `cd web && npm ci`.

**KEEP (real value):**
- URL query params as the only filter state, in `DashboardState`: parsing, defaults, invalid values, and round trips.
- Week logic in `week.ts`: Monday alignment, and the optional week inputs.
- The event-type guard.
- The user-facing copy from `health-copy.ts` that product owns: "usually X–Y" wording, status text, and insufficient-data messaging. One test per distinct copy rule.
- API client URLs and parameters that a real backend depends on.
- Component behaviour a user sees:
  - the location table's ranking order as rendered;
  - status labels;
  - empty, error and loading states;
  - account summary values;
  - filter changes updating the URL.
- The acceptance criteria UI-01 to UI-45 that carry real behaviour. See `docs/acceptance-criteria.md`.

**REMOVE:**
- Tests of Angular or framework behaviour:
  - "should create" smoke tests;
  - DI token wiring;
  - that a signal holds what was just set;
  - CSS class or markup trivia with no behaviour.
- Duplicates: the same rule asserted with trivially different inputs, or at both the unit and the component level when one is enough.
- Tests that just restate the implementation or check trivial pass-through code.

When several tests cover one rule, merge them into one table-driven `it.each`. If a fake or helper becomes unused, delete it.

**Rules:**
- Do not touch app code. Test files only.
- Be decisive.

**Verification:**
- `cd web && npm test`: everything passes. Give the before and after totals.
- `npx ng build`: succeeds.
- Commit. Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

**Report:** use the CLAUDE.md handoff format and include your branch name. Add:
1. A table with a row for every removed or merged test: test, action, and a one-line reason.
2. A short table mapping each kept behaviour area and UI criterion to the surviving test.

# CLAUDE.md — relay-activity-health

DASH-247: help a Relay customer admin answer "is this normal for us?" per account and per location. `PLAN.md` is the spec — read it before any work.
If a task conflicts with `PLAN.md`, stop and report; don't improvise.

## Stack
.NET 10 Minimal APIs · EF Core (schema, migrations, seed) · hand-written SQL for aggregates via `Database.SqlQuery<T>` · SQL Server 2022 (docker compose) ·
xUnit + Testcontainers · Angular (standalone, signals, URL query params as state) · Vitest.

## Non-negotiable code rules
1. **SOLID, no tight coupling.** Every class with behaviour (services, calculators, calendars, queries, API clients) depends on interfaces and is registered in DI.
   Records, DTOs, options and value objects are plain data — no interfaces for them. Angular: abstract-class DI tokens.
2. **No comment blocks. Forbidden.** No XML doc blocks, no banner comments, no multi-line explanations, no commented-out code.
   Code explains itself through names. A single-line comment only when the *why* is not expressible in code.
3. **Names are descriptive and domain-based**: `baselineWeeks`, `eligibleWeekCounts`, `latestCompleteWeekStart` — never `data`, `tmp`, `list2`, `x`.
4. **Test-first, per layer.** Interfaces + records + `NotImplementedException` stubs → the complete test suite (happy path + every edge case in PLAN §7) →
   commit **red** → user reviews the tests → implement to green → reviewer → next layer. Never write implementation and its tests in the same step.
5. **Test expectations come from PLAN.md** (§5.3 rules, §7 golden values), never from running the implementation.
6. C# test names are PascalCase without underscores (analyzer CA1707 stays on). Business-logic tests use no database and no mocks. SQL is tested only against real SQL Server (Testcontainers) — never EF InMemory or SQLite.
7. SQL does counting only (de-dup, bucket into given UTC windows, group). Week math, zero-fill, statistics and ranking live in `Relay.Core`.

## Boundaries
- `Relay.Core` references nothing else in the solution. `Relay.Infrastructure` implements Core's query interfaces. `Relay.Api` is the composition root.
- Only the `architect` edits public contracts (interfaces, records, API DTOs, TS models, abstract API tokens); it never scaffolds or edits project files.
  `backend` owns `.sln`, `*.csproj`, `Directory.*.props`, `global.json`; `frontend` owns `package.json`, `angular.json`.
  Anyone else who needs a contract, package or project change stops and reports it.
- `db/seed.sql` and `db/schema.sql` are never modified.
- Stay inside the file scope you were given.

## Working model
- The main thread is the coordinator: it dispatches subagents from `.claude/agents/`, reviews, merges, verifies. It does not write product code.
- Every agent task runs in its own git worktree — never on the main worktree; each subagent commits only its own scope, and the coordinator merges.
- After every feature lands, the `reviewer` reviews it and the owning agent fixes the findings. Findings that are unclear, conflict with PLAN.md, or need a product/design call go to the user before any fix.
- Every commit message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Endpoints call exactly one application service; they never inject query interfaces or `DbContext`.

## Handoff report (every agent, every task)
```
## Summary        one or two sentences: what was done
## Changed        paths created/edited
## Verification   exact commands run + trimmed output (never claim green without it)
## Deviations     anything that differs from PLAN.md/CLAUDE.md, and why
## Uncertain      interpretations you had to make; things the coordinator should check
## Next           what the next agent needs to know
```

## Commands
- DB: `docker compose up -d db`
- Backend tests: `dotnet test` (exits 8 while a test project has zero tests — expected until its red suite lands)
- API: `dotnet run --project src/Relay.Api` (fixed port **5080**; the Angular proxy targets it)
- Frontend: `cd web && npm start` · tests: `cd web && npm test`
- AI log export: `scripts/export-ai-log.sh`

- [Prefer libraries](prefer-libraries.md) — use a maintained library over hand-written code when one exists

## Summary
I cut the Angular Vitest suite from **243 tests to 124**, and all 124 pass. I deleted framework, pass-through and duplicate tests. Where several tests checked one rule, I merged them into a table-driven `it.each`. I added three small unit specs (`week`, `isEventType`, `health-copy`) and moved into them the checks that had been repeated at component and page level. No app code was touched. Branch: **`tests-prune-web`**, commit `c56cf56`.

## Changed
Everything is under `/Users/josemejia/Documents/Software Development/Qualitara/relay-activity-health/.claude/worktrees/agent-afa19de31000667a9/web/src/`.
- Deleted: `app/app.spec.ts`
- Rewritten: `app/core/api/accounts.api.spec.ts`, `app/core/api/activity-health.api.spec.ts`, `app/features/dashboard/dashboard-state.spec.ts`, `app/features/dashboard/dashboard.page.spec.ts`, `app/features/dashboard/components/{account-summary,dashboard-filters,location-table}.spec.ts`
- New: `app/features/dashboard/week.spec.ts`, `app/features/dashboard/event-type-guard.spec.ts`, `app/features/dashboard/health-copy.spec.ts`
- Unused helpers removed: `testing/router-testing.ts` (`currentPath`) and `testing/fake-apis.ts` (`FakeAccountsApi.listAccountsCalls`)

## Verification
- `npm test`, before: `Test Files 8 passed (8) · Tests 243 passed (243)`
- `npm test`, after: `Test Files 10 passed (10) · Tests 124 passed (124)`
  - Tests per file: accounts.api 1 · activity-health.api 2 · account-summary 2 · dashboard-filters 13 · location-table 5 · dashboard-state 24 · dashboard.page 45 · event-type-guard 6 · health-copy 14 · week 12
- `npx ng build`: `Application bundle generation complete`

## Deviations
- UI-42 asks for "a component test with count 1" for the singular nouns. That check is now in the unit test `health-copy.spec.ts` (`activityCount`), not in a component.
- I added new unit specs even though the task was to prune. They replace many component and page variants with 32 fast table rows, and cover the week and type rules you asked to keep.

## Uncertain
- Nine tests are stricter than before, all following the spec:
  - Eight rows of the normalisation table in `dashboard-state.spec.ts` now also check `replaceUrl`, no error, and that only valid types are sent to the API. Before, only some rows checked these.

  - All of these pass.
- Report fixtures that are only used inside `scenarioReports()` are still exported. They are live code, not dead.
